critiques.description: eas-035 treats map-024’s applicability and “unverified” status for req-DATA-001 as unsupported, even though evd-001 adequately supports both the applicability of the requirement and the choice of “unverified” given the documented data flow and missing encryption details.
critiques.rationale: evd-001 documents that field kiosks send customer order records, including names, delivery addresses, and order contents, over the store network to the Kiosk Sync Service, establishing a network transmission of customer personal data on this link (evd-001). Map-024 explicitly records as an assumption that this data is treated as confidential/restricted and, noting the absence of any documentation about encryption or integrity protection, sets satisfaction_status to “unverified” rather than asserting the control is absent. The fact that the source document does not name req-DATA-001 or thr-002 is a documentation gap, but it does not invalidate the inference that req-DATA-001 is applicable to this data flow or that its satisfaction is currently unverified based on the available evidence.

critiques.description: eas-036 classifies map-025 as unsupported because evd-001 does not explicitly label the Kiosk Sync Service as a “public interface,” even though the document clearly describes it as a client-facing service called by kiosks, which is sufficient to ground map-025’s non-applicability conclusion for req-NET-001.
critiques.rationale: evd-001 states that the Kiosk Sync Service “receives customer order records from the field kiosks” and that “the kiosks call it over the store network” (evd-001), which documents that this service is an endpoint directly invoked by remote clients. Map-025 reasonably interprets req-NET-001’s scope (internal components that are not public interfaces) and, with an explicit assumption about how “public interface” is defined for this catalog, concludes that req-NET-001 is not applicable to this threat path. Requiring system documentation to use the exact term “public interface by design” or to mention req-NET-001 explicitly before treating this as supported overstates the evidentiary requirement; the mapping’s conclusion is a permissible inference from the documented behavior of the service plus the requirement definition.
